title: Require documented training-data provenance and licensing review before deploying a generative model commercially
description: Illustrative reference decision modelled on the Getty Images v. Stability AI litigation. Not a documented decision of any specific organization.

history.note: Initial Phase 2A seed content, part of the Foundational Twenty.

Normalized US/UK spelling variants to the American-English house style (schema field names, e.g. organizations_involved, are already American; majority framework citations - NIST, FTC, EEOC, FCRA, BIPA - are American sources). decision_statement: Before a generative model is deployed commercially, the organization must document the provenance of its training data sources and complete a licensing review identifying any dataset obtained by scraping copyrighted or trademarked material, with a documented risk decision (license, exclude, or accept identified risk) for each source.
decision_context: Motivated by Getty Images v. Stability AI, in which a major generative image model's commercial deployment was challenged over its use of scraped, copyrighted training images without a license.
governing_body: Illustrative example — Generative Model Governance Board
alternatives_considered: Treat all publicly accessible training data as usable without a documented provenance review.
Address provenance questions only reactively, in response to a legal challenge.

citations.title: Getty Images (US) Inc and others v Stability AI Limited [2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch)
citations.publisher: Courts and Tribunals Judiciary (England and Wales High Court)

relationships.reason: This decision is modelled as a direct governance response to this litigation.
The decision is put into practice via this single, primary design pattern.
A documented provenance review is a concrete extension of this control's data-governance requirement to sourcing practices.
Compliance must be demonstrated by a documented training data provenance log.
Boards adopting this decision should be asking whether a defensible provenance record actually exists.
